title: VerbOntology
description: A canonical catalogue of action verbs, classified under KKO upper classes. Apple's AppIntent schema exposes 203 intents and only FOUR semantic verb primitives (`open`, `delete`, `search`, `audioStarting`); 156 of the 203 intents have no verb at all. That thinness is not a design choice, it is an absence — a system with no verb ontology cannot say why two actions are the same kind of thing. This ontology anchors each verb in the KKO upper structure (see PROVENANCE.md), so a `send` and a `publish` are both `Communication` (a form of TriadicAction — one event produces a second that mediates a third), and a `read` and a `list` are both `Observation` under Events. Classifications are decisions, not scrapings; they must be traceable to the KKO class name.

kkoVersion.description: Version of KKO the upper-class references anchor to. Locks provenance so a widening of KKO upstream is visible as a version bump here.

id.description: Stable lowercase ASCII identifier — the primary key. Verbs are named for what they DO, not for the tool that implements them.

definition.description: What the verb means in one sentence. Prose only — the machine-checkable content lives in kkoClass.

kkoClass.description: The KKO upper class this verb specialises. Not free text — the classifier lists the acceptable values.

voice.description: actor: verb describes what a subject DOES (send, delete). patient: what happens TO a subject (received, deleted). observer: pure inspection (read, list, count) that does not modify. Apple’s vocabulary conflates all three; keeping them apart is what lets a governance layer decide when a receipt is required.

reversibleByDefault.description: Default reversibility for actions specialising this verb. Individual action entries may still override (e.g. a specific `send` variant that can be recalled).

aliases.description: Other names people call this verb — kept for search, never for identity. The id is authoritative; an alias is a lookup convenience.
